messages:
maria_ng: heads up — onboarding a quantized 13B on A100s is showing a weird p95 regression in us-west vs europe-west despite same SKU. saw this after the v2 quant run.
josh_t: can you paste the numbers? is this latency or tail variance only?
maria_ng: p50 ~ 120ms both regions, but p95 in us-west ~ 430ms and eu-west ~ 220ms. throughput (tokens/s) comparable. suspect driver/CUDA stack difference. stack diffs below from node metadata:

```
us-west: Ubuntu 20.04 | nvidia-driver 525.85 | cuda 12.1 | libcudnn 8.9
eu-west: Ubuntu 20.04 | nvidia-driver 535.86 | cuda 12.2 | libcudnn 8.10
```

maria_ng: also seeing more frequent small stalls in the server logs (KV cache flushes?) — snippet:

```
[2026-02-10T14:22:31Z] WARN serve: wait_for_kernel: launch took 12.4ms (threshold 5ms)
[2026-02-10T14:22:31Z] INFO runtime: kv_cache_miss: 1.4% requests
```

samir_k: hmm that's a pretty big driver diff. 525 -> 535 could change cublas/cuBLASLt heuristics and kernel selection for fp4/q4 matmuls. did you run with the same kernel selection flags?
maria_ng: yes, same runtime flags: --matmul-backend=auto --force-kernel-v=0. flags file attached in release build.
claire_ml: could be a fallback to a slower kernel in that driver combo. we saw similar with an older CUDA where small batch gemm fell back to different algorithm. try forcing the new kernel path and repro.

josh_t: quick microbenchmark we use:
```
python perf_gemm.py --dtype q4 --m 2048 --n 128 --k 4096 --reps 500
```
that should highlight kernel dispatch variance.

maria_ng: ran that on both regions, results:
```
us-west: avg 0.85ms, p95 2.3ms
eu-west: avg 0.82ms, p95 0.9ms
```
shows tail in us-west.

infra-bot: FYI — node image in us-west rolled from gpu-image-2026-02-01 -> gpu-image-2026-02-08 on 2026-02-09 03:10 UTC (automated).

samir_k: could be a kernel regression introduced in 525 -> 535 or packaging quirk in the image. two quick actions:
- pin driver to 535 on a us-west test node and rerun
- build a local runtime with cublas Lt fallback disabled to force the optimized matmul path

claire_ml: also, check NUMA/SM affinity — some clouds default different CPU->GPU pinning; that can cause small stalls that show up as p95. run `nvidia-smi topo --matrix` and `numactl --hardware` on both nodes.

maria_ng: good call. I checked topo earlier — identical PCI connectivity, but CPU governor was different (performance vs ondemand). changing governor fixed ~30ms of the tail in a quick test.

josh_t: ok so we have two contributing factors: driver/kernel dispatch and CPU governor/NIC interrupt coalescing. for final repro plan:
1) repro on us-west test node with driver 535 and perf governor
2) run perf_gemm and full inference q13b trace
3) if still tail-heavy, build runtime with `--matmul-backend=cublaslt` and `--disable-fallback` and test

maria_ng: will run the plan and post results here. thanks y'all — tagging @infra for a temporary driver pin on the test pool :infra-team:

infra-bot: @infra-team notified. created ticket INF-4923 to pin nvidia-driver=535.86 on pool redwood-ml-usw-test.

maria_ng: quick update — after pin + perf governor, p95 dropped to ~230ms and gemm p95 -> 1.0ms. still a hair higher than eu-west but acceptable for canary. keeping this open until we confirm rollout safety.

claire_ml: excellent. when you have the full traces, let's run the eval comparison (quality/latency) and add a regression alert for p95 > 300ms on that route.

maria_ng: will do, uploading traces shortly. thanks! :thumbsup!
